question: What were the coins minted in Delhi during the reign of Tomar and Chauhan called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dehliwal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The coins minted at Delhi during the rule of the Tomars and Chauhans were known as Dehliwal (देहलीवाल).

• These were largely bull-and-horseman type billon (silver-copper alloy) coins that circulated widely in the region around Delhi.

• The Dehliwal continued in use even after the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate before being replaced by new coinage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Tomars are traditionally credited with founding Dhillika (Delhi), later taken over by the Chauhans (Chahamanas) under Prithviraj Chauhan.

• Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate is credited with introducing the standard silver Tanka and copper Jital.

• Coins are a vital source for reconstructing the political and economic history of early medieval India.

NOTE

• Rupees (Option 1): A silver coin standardised by Sher Shah Suri (the 'Rupiya'), much later than the Tomar-Chauhan period.

• Dinar (Option 3): A gold coin term of Roman/Arabic origin; used for high-value gold currency, not the Tomar-Chauhan issue.

• Tanka (Option 4): The standard silver coin introduced by Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate.

question: What was the 'zat' in the Mughal mansabdari system?
option_1: It determined the land a mansabdar was given.
option_2: It was the numerical value determining a noble's rank and salary
option_3: It referred to the military responsibilities assigned to a noble.
option_4: It was a tax imposed on the mansabdars.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It was the numerical value determining a noble's rank and salary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Mughal mansabdari system (मनसबदारी व्यवस्था), every officer (mansabdar) held a rank called mansab expressed by two numbers — zat and sawar.

• The zat (जात) fixed the mansabdar's personal rank, status and salary in the imperial hierarchy.

• The sawar indicated the number of horsemen (cavalry) the mansabdar was required to maintain.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The mansabdari system was introduced by Emperor Akbar.

• Mansabdars were paid either in cash (naqd) or through the assignment of revenue land called jagir.

• Ranks ranged from 10 up to 5,000 for nobles, and higher for princes of royal blood.

NOTE

• It determined the land a mansabdar was given (Option 1): Land assignment for salary was the jagir, not the zat.

• It referred to the military responsibilities assigned to a noble (Option 3): The cavalry/military obligation was indicated by the sawar rank.

• It was a tax imposed on the mansabdars (Option 4): Zat was a rank, not a tax.

question: The Indian Ocean Rim Association was established in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) (हिंद महासागर रिम संघ) was established in 1997 at Mauritius.

• It is an inter-governmental organisation aimed at strengthening regional cooperation and sustainable development in the Indian Ocean region.

• It was originally known as the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation (IOR-ARC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• IORA's Secretariat is located at Ebene, Mauritius.

• It works on priority areas such as maritime safety, trade and investment facilitation, fisheries management, disaster risk management and tourism.

• India has been an active founding member of IORA.

NOTE

• 1983 (Option 1): Not the year of IORA's establishment.

• 2003 (Option 3): Not related to IORA's founding.

• 2008 (Option 4): Not related to IORA's founding.

question: Who was first woman Chief Minister of any state in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sucheta Kripalani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sucheta Kripalani (सुचेता कृपलानी) became the first woman Chief Minister of any Indian state.

• She served as the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 1963 to 1967.

• She was a prominent freedom fighter and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She was married to socialist leader Acharya J. B. Kripalani.

• She sang 'Vande Mataram' in the Constituent Assembly just before Jawaharlal Nehru's 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on 15 August 1947.

• India's first woman Prime Minister was Indira Gandhi (1966).

NOTE

• Aruna Asaf Ali (Option 1): A freedom fighter famous for hoisting the flag during the 1942 Quit India Movement; first Mayor of Delhi.

• Anna Chandy (Option 3): India's first woman judge and first woman High Court judge.

• Kamala Nehru (Option 4): Freedom activist and wife of Jawaharlal Nehru; never a Chief Minister.

question: Who among the following was the first female recipient of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asima Chatterjee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Asima Chatterjee (असीमा चटर्जी) was the first woman to receive the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, in 1961.

• She was an eminent organic chemist known for her work on vinca alkaloids and anti-epileptic and anti-malarial drugs.

• The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize is India's premier award in science and technology, given by CSIR.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She was the first woman to be awarded a Doctorate of Science (D.Sc.) by an Indian university (University of Calcutta).

• She was also the first woman elected as General President of the Indian Science Congress Association.

• The Bhatnagar Prize is named after Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, the founder-director of CSIR.

NOTE

• Debala Mitra (Option 1): A noted archaeologist and Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

• Sudipta Sengupta (Option 3): A structural geologist and one of the first Indian women to visit Antarctica.

• Archana Bhattacharyya (Option 4): A geophysicist and former Director of the Indian Institute of Geomagnetism.

question: In 2024, at the National Film Awards, the Best Music Direction (Songs) award was presented to ____ for his work on Brahmastra - Part 1: Shiva (Hindi).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pritam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 70th National Film Awards (2024), the Best Music Direction (Songs) (सर्वश्रेष्ठ संगीत निर्देशन - गीत) award went to Pritam for Brahmastra Part 1: Shiva.

• Pritam Chakraborty is a leading Indian Bollywood music composer.

• The film Brahmastra was directed by Ayan Mukerji and released in 2022.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the same 70th National Film Awards, the Best Music Direction (Background Score) went to A. R. Rahman for Ponniyin Selvan: Part 1.

• The National Film Awards are administered by the Directorate of Film Festivals (now under NFDC).

• The awards are presented annually by the President of India.

NOTE

• Mahesh Bhuvanend (Option 2): Not the recipient of this award for Brahmastra.

• Niki Joshi (Option 3): Not the recipient of this award.

• Ravi Varman (Option 4): A cinematographer, not the winner of the Best Music Direction (Songs) award.

question: 50th Statehood Day of a state was celebrated in May 2025. Prem Singh Tamang (P.S. Golay) is Chief Minister of this state. Which state is being discussed here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sikkim (सिक्किम) celebrated its 50th Statehood Day in May 2025, having become a full-fledged state of India on 16 May 1975.

• Prem Singh Tamang (P.S. Golay) of the Sikkim Krantikari Morcha (SKM) is the Chief Minister of Sikkim.

• Sikkim was the 22nd state to join the Indian Union.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The capital of Sikkim is Gangtok.

• Sikkim is India's least populous state and shares borders with Nepal, Bhutan and China.

• Kanchenjunga, the highest peak in India, lies in Sikkim.

NOTE

• Mizoram (Option 2): Became a state in 1987; its Chief Minister is not P.S. Golay.

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3): Became a state in 1987, not 1975.

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Became a state in 1972; not linked to P.S. Golay.

question: In July 2024, which country recently conferred its highest civilian award "The Order of St. Andrew the Apostle" to Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Russia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2024, Russia (रूस) conferred its highest civilian honour, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle, on Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• The award was presented during PM Modi's visit to Moscow for the India-Russia Annual Summit.

• The honour was originally announced in 2019 for his contribution to India-Russia relations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Order of St. Andrew the Apostle is the highest state decoration of the Russian Federation.

• PM Modi has received the highest civilian awards of several countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Palestine, Afghanistan, Maldives, Bahrain, Bhutan and the USA.

• The award was presented by Russian President Vladimir Putin.

NOTE

• France (Option 1): Its highest honour is the Legion of Honour (Grand Cross conferred on PM Modi in 2023).

• Croatia (Option 2): Did not confer the Order of St. Andrew.

• Ghana (Option 3-listed): Ghana conferred the Officer of the Order of the Star of Ghana on PM Modi in 2025, not the Order of St. Andrew.

question: According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, India's overall female labour force participation rate (FLFPR) has risen to _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 41.7%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24 (आवधिक श्रम बल सर्वेक्षण), India's overall Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR) for ages 15+ rose to 41.7%.

• This marked a notable rise from 37.0% in the previous year.

• The overall LFPR (15+) increased to 60.1%, with male participation at 78.8%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PLFS is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• PLFS was launched in 2017 to provide estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators.

• It measures LFPR, Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate.

NOTE

• 11.7% (Option 1): Understates the actual figure; not correct.

• 31.7% (Option 2): Incorrect figure for FLFPR in PLFS 2023-24.

• 51.7% (Option 3): Overstates the actual figure; not correct.

question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, a revamped UDAN initiative will be launched to further enhance regional connectivity, adding _____ new destinations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 120.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26 (केंद्रीय बजट), Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a modified/revamped UDAN scheme to add 120 new destinations.

• The scheme aims to carry an estimated 4 crore additional passengers over the next decade.

• UDAN stands for Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik and is the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The modified UDAN will support helipads and smaller airports in hilly, aspirational and North-Eastern districts.

• The original UDAN scheme was launched in 2016 to make air travel affordable for common citizens.

• It follows a market-based mechanism with viability gap funding for airlines.

NOTE

• 155 (Option 2): Not the figure announced in the Budget 2025-26.

• 95 (Option 3): Incorrect number of new destinations.

• 165 (Option 4): Incorrect number of new destinations.

question: As of October 2024, which of the following is not recognized as a category under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yuva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) (प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना), loans are classified into categories named Shishu, Kishor and Tarun.

• Yuva is not a category under PMMY.

• A new category, Tarun Plus (loans above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh), was introduced in 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shishu covers loans up to Rs 50,000; Kishor covers above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh; Tarun covers above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh.

• PMMY was launched in April 2015 to provide collateral-free institutional credit to micro and small enterprises.

• Loans are provided through MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency).

NOTE

• Shishu (Option 1): A valid PMMY category for loans up to Rs 50,000.

• Kishor (Option 2): A valid PMMY category for loans above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh.

• Tarun (Option 3): A valid PMMY category for loans above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh.

question:
Narcotics are used as doping in sports. Which of the following is an example of narcotics?
I. Morphine
II. Methadone
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Morphine and Methadone are examples of narcotics (नशीले पदार्थ) that are prohibited in sports as doping agents.

• Narcotics are opioid analgesics that suppress pain and can be misused to mask injuries and enhance performance.

• They fall under the substances banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other prohibited narcotics include heroin, fentanyl, oxycodone and pethidine.

• WADA maintains the annually updated Prohibited List of substances and methods.

• India's national anti-doping body is NADA (National Anti-Doping Agency).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since Methadone is also a narcotic.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since Morphine is also a narcotic.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both are narcotics.

question: A badminton match generally consists games of _____ points each
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A standard badminton (बैडमिंटन) match is played in a best-of-three games format, with each game played up to 21 points.

• A player/pair must win by a margin of at least 2 points; if the score reaches 20-20, play continues until one side leads by 2.

• The maximum score in a game is capped at 30 points (the side reaching 30 first wins).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The rally point scoring system (21 points) was adopted by the BWF in 2006, replacing the earlier 15-point system.

• The sport is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).

• A point is scored on every serve (rally point scoring).

NOTE

• 17 (Option 1): Not the standard points-per-game in badminton.

• 19 (Option 2): Not the standard points-per-game in badminton.

• 23 (Option 4): Not the standard points-per-game in badminton.

question: Which state government has launched Majhi Vasundhara Campaign 6.0 to strengthen environmental conservation efforts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Maharashtra (महाराष्ट्र) government launched the Majhi Vasundhara Campaign 6.0 to strengthen environmental conservation.

• 'Majhi Vasundhara' means 'My Earth', and the campaign focuses on the five elements — Earth, Water, Air, Fire and Sky (Panchatatva).

• It promotes citizen participation in tackling climate change at the local body level.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The campaign was first launched in 2020-21 by Maharashtra's Environment and Climate Change Department.

• The capital of Maharashtra is Mumbai.

• The campaign encourages tree plantation, renewable energy adoption and waste management.

NOTE

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Did not launch the Majhi Vasundhara Campaign.

• Sikkim (Option 3): Not associated with this campaign.

• Manipur (Option 4): Not associated with this campaign.

question: Which country hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qatar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Qatar (कतर) hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022, the 22nd edition of the tournament.

• It was the first Arab/Middle-Eastern nation to host the FIFA World Cup, held in November-December 2022.

• Argentina won the title, defeating France on penalties in the final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The final was played at the Lusail Stadium.

• Lionel Messi won the Golden Ball (best player); Kylian Mbappe won the Golden Boot.

• The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico.

• Spain (Option 3): A co-host of the 2030 FIFA World Cup, not 2022.

question: FIFA Men's U-17 World Cup 2025 will be held in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qatar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIFA Men's U-17 World Cup 2025 (फीफा पुरुष अंडर-17 विश्व कप) is being held in Qatar.

• Qatar will host the tournament annually from 2025 to 2029 under an agreement with FIFA.

• The tournament features an expanded field of 48 teams.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

• The matches are being played at the Aspire Zone facilities in Doha.

• India hosted the FIFA U-17 World Cup in 2017.

• Spain (Option 3): Not the host of the U-17 World Cup 2025.

question: 'Guruvayur' festival is native festival of which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Guruvayur (गुरुवायूर) festival is a native festival of Kerala.

• It is associated with the famous Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple in Thrissur district.

• The temple is one of the most important Krishna (Guruvayurappan) shrines in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Guruvayur Ekadasi and the annual Utsavam (elephant race - Aanayottam) are major highlights.

• Kerala's capital is Thiruvananthapuram.

• Other famous festivals of Kerala include Onam, Thrissur Pooram and Vishu.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for festivals like Navratri and Rann Utsav, not Guruvayur.

• Assam (Option 3): Known for Bihu, not Guruvayur.

• Tripura (Option 4): Known for festivals like Kharchi Puja, not Guruvayur.

question: The Gol Gumbaz the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gol Gumbaz (गोल गुम्बज) is the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah, located at Bijapur (Vijayapura) in Karnataka.

• It is famous for having one of the largest domes in the world.

• It was built in the 17th century in the Deccan (Indo-Islamic) architectural style.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Gol Gumbaz has a famous 'Whispering Gallery' where even faint sounds echo clearly.

• Mohammed Adil Shah belonged to the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur.

• Karnataka's capital is Bengaluru.

NOTE

• Delhi (Option 1): Home to monuments like Humayun's Tomb and the Red Fort, not the Gol Gumbaz.

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Home to the Taj Mahal (Agra), not the Gol Gumbaz.

• Telangana (Option 4): Home to the Charminar (Hyderabad), not the Gol Gumbaz.

question: What is the name of Blue Origin's first orbital rocket launched in January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Glenn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• New Glenn was Blue Origin's first orbital rocket, which made its debut launch in January 2025.

• It is a heavy-lift, partially reusable launch vehicle named after astronaut John Glenn.

• Blue Origin is the private space company founded by Jeff Bezos.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• New Glenn stands about 98 metres tall and is designed with a reusable first stage.

• Blue Origin's earlier suborbital vehicle, New Shepard, is used for space tourism.

• Its main competitor is SpaceX's reusable Falcon rockets.

NOTE

• New Shepard (Option 1): Blue Origin's suborbital rocket used for space tourism, named after Alan Shepard.

• New Horizon (Option 2): New Horizons is a NASA space probe to Pluto, not a Blue Origin rocket.

• Blue Moon (Option 4): Blue Origin's lunar lander, not an orbital rocket.

question: Why we are not crushed under the large atmospheric pressure?
option_3: Because atmospheric pressure is very low
option_4: Because the pressure inside our body balances the outside pressure
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because the pressure inside our body balances the outside pressure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We are not crushed by atmospheric pressure because the internal pressure of our body balances the external atmospheric pressure (वायुमंडलीय दाब).

• The blood and fluids inside our body exert an outward pressure equal to the air pressure pushing inward.

• This balance of internal and external pressure keeps the body stable.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101.3 kPa (1 atmosphere), roughly 10^5 Pascal.

• Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer, invented by Evangelista Torricelli.

• Pressure decreases with increasing altitude.

NOTE

• Because we are very strong (Option 1): Human strength is unrelated to withstanding air pressure.

• Because gravity pulls it away (Option 2): Gravity actually causes atmospheric pressure; it does not pull it away.

• Because atmospheric pressure is very low (Option 3): Atmospheric pressure is substantial (about 1 atm), not very low.

question: Which of the following fort was built by Suraj Mal in Bharatpur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lohagarh Fort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lohagarh Fort (लोहागढ़ किला) in Bharatpur (Rajasthan) was built by Maharaja Suraj Mal of the Jat dynasty.

• 'Lohagarh' means 'Iron Fort', so named because of its strength and its ability to withstand repeated British attacks.

• It is one of the few forts that remained undefeated by the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Maharaja Suraj Mal is often called the 'Plato of the Jat community' and was the ruler of Bharatpur in the 18th century.

• The fort has structures like Kishori Mahal, Mahal Khas and Moti Mahal.

• Bharatpur is also famous for the Keoladeo National Park (a bird sanctuary).

NOTE

• Amer Fort (Option 1): Located in Jaipur, built by Raja Man Singh I.

• Agra Fort (Option 2): Located in Agra, associated with Akbar and the Mughals.

• Red Fort (Option 4): Located in Delhi, built by Shah Jahan.

question:
Which of the following pairs of revenue system – person who devised it is correct?
I. Mahalwari settlement- Holt Mackenzie
II. Ryotwari system- Alexander Read and Thomas Munro
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both statements are correct. The Mahalwari settlement (महालवारी बंदोबस्त) was devised by Holt Mackenzie (1822).

• The Ryotwari system (रैयतवारी व्यवस्था) was devised by Alexander Read and Thomas Munro.

• These were land-revenue systems introduced by the British in different parts of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the Mahalwari system, revenue was assessed on the 'mahal' (village or estate) as a unit; it was implemented in the North-Western Provinces, parts of Central India and Punjab.

• In the Ryotwari system, revenue was collected directly from individual cultivators (ryots), mainly in Madras and Bombay Presidencies.

• The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari system) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 in Bengal.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both pairs are correctly matched.

question: What is the minimum age to become a member of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha (राज्यसभा) is 30 years.

• This is laid down under Article 84(b) of the Constitution of India.

• The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House (Council of States) of the Indian Parliament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every two years.

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• 25 (Option 1): The minimum age for Lok Sabha membership, not Rajya Sabha.

• 35 (Option 3): The minimum age required to become President or Vice-President of India.

• 21 (Option 4): The minimum voting age in India, not an eligibility age for Rajya Sabha.

question: Which of the following part of brain has separate areas specialized for hearing, smell, sight, etc.?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fore brain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fore brain (अग्रमस्तिष्क) is the main thinking part of the brain and has separate areas specialized for hearing, smell, sight, etc.

• It contains sensory reception areas that receive impulses from various sense organs.

• The cerebrum, the largest part of the fore brain, controls voluntary actions and intelligence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three major parts of the human brain are the fore brain, mid brain and hind brain.

• The hind brain includes the cerebellum, pons and medulla oblongata.

• The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like heartbeat and breathing.

NOTE

• Mid brain (Option 2): Connects the fore brain and hind brain and controls reflex movements of the head, neck and eyes.

• Hind brain (Option 3): Includes the cerebellum (balance and coordination) and medulla (involuntary actions).

• Spinal cord (Option 4): Part of the central nervous system responsible for reflex actions, not a part of the brain.

question: The grammar composed by Panini consists of over _____ grammatical rules.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The grammar composed by Panini (पाणिनि), known as the Ashtadhyayi, consists of nearly 4000 grammatical rules (sutras).

• Panini was an ancient Sanskrit grammarian, regarded as the 'Father of Linguistics'.

• The Ashtadhyayi is one of the most systematic and scientific works of grammar in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 'Ashtadhyayi' literally means 'eight chapters' (ashta = eight, adhyaya = chapter).

• Panini is believed to have lived around the 5th-4th century BCE, in the region of Gandhara.

• His work laid the foundation for the study of Sanskrit grammar and modern linguistics.

NOTE

• 692 (Option 1): Understates the number of sutras in the Ashtadhyayi.

• 1632 (Option 2): Not the accepted figure for Panini's rules.

• 7012 (Option 4): Overstates the number of rules in the Ashtadhyayi.
